To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a compact XML-based content model for representing human-conceived analogics and have designed a system that allows analogy authors to express their analogies using this model, and allows end users to visualize, retrieve, and rank these analogies.

(1) we developed a compact XML analogy expression markup language that is capable of representing human-conceived analogical expressions; (2) we developed methods for visualizing and ranking such expressions; and (3) we developed a Web-based system, MARVIN, that provides a medium for analogy practitioners to represent, retrieve, visualize, and share human-conceived analogues.

a simple XML content model for analogies is capable of representing the wide range of human conceived analogies, that a Web-based system that provides this model and a set of tools for visualizing, retrieving, and storing such analogies can be useful to analogy authors and analogy end users, and that such a system is scalable to large archives of analogy expressions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the representation, visualization, and retrieval of analogy expressions.
the design and development of a Web-based system that can represent, retrieve, and visualize analogies in a manner that is useful to analogy practitioners.
developing methods for the representation, retrieval, and visualization of human-conceived analogy expressions in Web-based environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MARVIN is a valuable tool that provides a medium for analogy authors and end-users to express, share, and retrieve analogies in a common language.
MARVIN provides an excellent foundation upon which to build a Web-based system to support analogy practitioners.
we are pleased with the MARVIN system and believe that it is useful to the analogy research community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed, implemented, and evaluated an effective and efficient Web-based system for storing and retrieving analogies.
we have developed a system for representing, visualizing, and retrieving human-conceived analogical expressions, and that this system is of value to analogy researchers and practitioners.
we have developed a system that can be used to share analogies in a Web-based environment, and that it is capable of supporting the needs of analogy authors, end users, and developers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Web can be used to support the sharing and reuse of human-conceived analogy expressions.
a common language and a common medium for analogy expression can facilitate sharing of analogies and their use in a wide variety of applications.
a Web-based system like MARVIN can provide a useful medium for analogy practitioners to represent, share, and retrieve human-conceived analogical expressions.
